label: Q-24
title: UniPoolerCutoverEscrow exit/seed sandwich value-leak hypothesis refuted on fork (attacker net-negative); residual: by documented design (story-052 L223) price protection is off-chain -- minAmountsOut checked only length==2 and >0 (1 wei passes, token order unvalidated) and the V2 seed inherits the Balancer spot composition with no ratio/peg band
description:
The seed ratio is whatever composition the Balancer pool has at exit, and story-103's floors are quoted from live state. So a pre-skewed Balancer pool would be baked into both the floors and the V2 seed price. Checked against mainnet: the pool is a 50/50 weighted pool, which is constant-product like V2, with no hooks and a 0.3% fee. For two constant-product venues an LP position's value at a given price depends only on its invariant. If an attacker skews the Balancer price and the escrow exits and seeds at the skewed price, arbitraging both venues back returns the attacker roughly their own slippage, minus 0.3% fees on each leg. POL is not extracted. Hookless pool: no V3 hook can adjust amounts or call back. Residual risk is limited to wrong-order or loose floors (PATTERN-002). The escrow cannot check order, so the core should assert getPoolTokenInfo order [sUSDS, phUSD] when building minAmountsOut.

On-chain validation of minAmountsOut is minimal: length==2 and each >0, so 1 wei passes and token order is unvalidated; the seed inherits the Balancer spot composition with no ratio or peg band.
impact: None demonstrated. On fork, a sandwich that skews the Balancer pool inside the floors is net-negative for the attacker (-1.753 sUSDS at 1% tol, -8.808 sUSDS at 5%). The protocol's seeded invariant rises slightly (+0.96 / +4.82 sUSDS at p0).
failureScenario: No value-extracting scenario. Hypothesis tested: attacker pre-skews the Balancer pool inside the floors, exitAndSeed exits and seeds at the skewed ratio, attacker back-arbitrages both venues. Fork result: attacker PnL -1.753 sUSDS (1% tol) / -8.808 sUSDS (5% tol); protocol seeded invariant rises (+0.96 / +4.82 sUSDS at p0).
assumptions: The Balancer pool stays a hookless 50/50 weighted pool with a 0.3% fee (verified on-chain). A pool type with a different curve or hooks would reopen the question.

relatedWontFix.L-06: 342075dfba3c8ec7c3bae1ae18c357591c5ea255bf649ee943c6c71f3ddd4c2e (wont-fix; its triageReason says 'If BalancerPoolerV2 is NOT retired, or is re-used by new code, this disposition should be revisited' -- revisited here, conclusion QA)

severityJustification: On-chain validation of minAmountsOut is minimal: length==2 and >0, so 1 wei passes and token order is unvalidated. The seed inherits the Balancer spot composition with no ratio or peg band. These are spec and defense-in-depth gaps, not a value leak: two constant-product venues mean the back-arbitrage returns only the attacker's own slippage minus fees, and POL is not extracted (ECON-001, CODE-003). Per the L-22/L-06 tolerance precedent, the floors bound accepted MEV on protocol-owned liquidity. Not suppressed under L-06 because L-06's own triageReason says new code reusing the pool should be revisited. It was revisited here and the conclusion is QA. PATTERN-002/003's mechanical 'potential-high' did not set the label. Off-chain price protection is the documented design (story-052 L223: minAmountsOut is the exit's slippage guard), not a defect.
recommendedMitigation: In UniPoolerCutoverCore, assert getPoolTokenInfo order == [sUSDS, phUSD] when building minAmountsOut. Optionally add an on-chain ratio band on the seed.
pocNote: No H/M this run: no PoC requirement. Fork tests listed under evidence are the supporting proof.
